newsitem.title: MEXICO: Gruma to invest $50 mln in bread plant.
newsitem.headline: Gruma to invest $50 mln in bread plant.

text.p: Mexican tortilla and corn flour maker Gruma SA de CV said on Wednesday it would invest $50 million in the construction of its first bread factory for products to be launched under the brand name Breddy.

"The plant will serve primarily the northeast of the country and the investment will be $50 million," Javier Velez, Gruma's chief financial officer, told Reuters. "Thirty percent will be spent this year with the rest next year."
Gruma, which holds a large chunk of the U.S. and Central American tortilla and corn flour markets, is the holding company for Grupo Industrial Maseca (Maseca), Mexico's dominant corn flour producer.

The bread plant, to be built near the northern industrial city of Monterrey, where Gruma and Maseca are headquartered, will make loaf bread, hot dog and hamburger buns, sweet rolls and possibly snacks like corn chips, Velez said.
Although the plant's precise site has not been determined, the company hopes to complete construction within 15 months, Velez said.

"The bread initially will be made in Monterrey, that's the first phase, and later we'll try to expand the same concept nationwide," Velez said. "We're starting in Monterrey because here is where there are the highest rates of consumption for packaged tortillas."
The plant will turn out about 40,000 tonnes a year and employ about 200 workers at capacity, he said.

Gruma currently makes bread in Los Angeles and Costa Rica, where it is a market leader, Velez said, and the company aims to gain 30 percent of the Mexican market within five years. ((--Jacqueline Lerma, Monterrey bureau, +528 345-7677))
